title: Bento-box triage & sprint prio plan (console UX)
body:
Context:
This is the working doc from the July 12 triage workshop — we used a "bento-box" mental model to group console/tooling intake into four lanes: Visibility, Controls, Onboarding, and Ops. Purpose is to produce a lean, testable sprint slice for the next two-week sprint and generate a small cutset for a possible hotfix sprint if we need to meet Q3 goals.

Workshop takeaways (high level):
- Keep the intake surface minimal: only three required fields for any new console route (name, intent, customer-impact). Everything else should be optional metadata.
- Prioritize endpoints that recover from regressions automatically (fallback routing) and expose per-route cost telemetry in the UI.
- Wireframe idea: a compact route card that expands in-place to show rollouts, tracing links, and last-24h cost delta.
- UX constraint: maintain keyboard-first triage flows for SRE and SEs (quick accept/reject keyboard shortcuts).

Triage matrix (Bento lanes):
1) Visibility (observability + dashboards)
   - Rationale: Most customer escalations begin with "I can't see what the model did". Low risk, high impact.
   - Candidate tickets: RWI-4521 (route cost ribbon), RWI-4590 (per-token latency breakdown), RWI-4628 (trace-to-span deep link)
   - Wireframe notes: compact route card includes sparkline + cost delta + last-run status badge. Expand->show top 3 recent errors and link to traces.
   - Priority: P0 for Sprint A (testable backend + small UI card).

2) Controls (rollouts, fallbacks, policies)
   - Rationale: Reduces blast radius during model rollouts. Higher product complexity and backend dependency.
   - Candidate tickets: RWI-4612 (canary toggle UI), RWI-4634 (fallback policy editor), RWI-4641 (model pinning quick action)
   - Wireframe notes: lightweight modal for rollout edits; allow "quick rollback" button on route card. UX needs guardrails (confirm + audit reason).
   - Priority: P1 for Sprint A (defer complex editors to Sprint B), P0 for hotfix if a rollout incident occurs.

3) Onboarding (templates, quickstart routes, examples)
   - Rationale: Reduces support overhead and time-to-first-success for new users. Usually high ROI but lower urgency.
   - Candidate tickets: RWI-4683 (route templates gallery), RWI-4700 (cli-to-console flow), RWI-4712 (starter prompt packs)
   - Wireframe notes: full-width gallery panel with filter chips (use-case, model family, latency profile).
   - Priority: P2 for Sprint A (shippable later).

4) Ops (infrastructure controls, capacity knobs)
   - Rationale: Required for Dedicated/Private customers. Backend-heavy.
   - Candidate tickets: RWI-4559 (capacity preview), RWI-4572 (autoscale dry-run), RWI-4740 (kms-policy status)
   - Wireframe notes: inline preview with estimated cost delta; small "simulate" tool to run a capacity change and show impact.
   - Priority: P1 (backend spike this sprint).

Sprint slice proposal (2-week):
- Goals: ship compact route card + cost ribbon + quick expand with traces link (Visibility lane).
- Acceptance criteria (AC):
  1) Route card shows name, intent, last-24h cost delta, 7d sparkline, and status badge.
  2) Expand reveals top 3 errors with link to trace (opens in new tab).
  3) Keyboard shortcuts: press 'e' to expand focused card, 'r' to open rollout modal.
  4) Backend provides an endpoint /routes/:id/summary with cost + errors (mocked for now).
- Rough estimates: FE 8pts, BE 5pts, QA 3pts, total 16pts.
- Owners: FE - Tomas Rivera, BE - Samir Patel, QA - Jin Park, PM - Maya Chen.

Hotfix cutset (minimal):
- If we need an emergency ship for customer X: deliver read-only route card + trace links + cost delta (no expand).
- Cutset story points: FE 3pts, BE 2pts, total 5pts.

Wireframe quick notes (textual):
- Card collapsed (w/ keyboard focus) shows: [route name] — [intent tag] — [status badge: green/yellow/red] — [cost delta: +$12 / -$3] — [7d sparkline].
- On expand: 3 columns: left=last 3 deploys (time, version), middle=errors (message, count, link), right=rollout controls (view + quick rollback).
- Modal patterns: keep it single-column on mobile; avoid deep nested tabs.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Do we allow non-admins to trigger quick rollback? (security vs speed). Action: confirm with security team.
- How granular should cost delta be (per-route vs per-customer-per-route)? MVP: per-route only.
- Are traces allowed to include customer PII? Work with privacy team to redact.

Dependencies and blockers:
- Backend needs a summary endpoint; currently planned for mid-sprint by platform-engineering (spike requested). Blocker RWI-4705 (auth headers for summary API) must be unblocked.
- Telemetry team needs to expose per-route cost metric in Prometheus; ticket RWI-4521 is already in their backlog.

Next steps / action items (owner in parens):
- Tomas: create FE prototype (storybook) for compact route card by Jul 16.
- Samir: spike on /routes/:id/summary endpoint + auth flow by Jul 14.
- Maya: draft release notes + customer-facing screenshot for support by Jul 18.
- Jin: write three QA smoke tests for collapsed/expand flows by Jul 19.
- Maya: schedule follow-up with security and telemetry on Jul 15 (invite list: security, telemetry, platform-eng).

Notes to self (informal):
- This feels like a candidate for "gradual rollout" in the Console — start read-only -> expand -> controls in subsequent sprint.
- Keep copy terse; operators want minimal noise. Use icons for status + small tooltips.

Appendix: sample short Jira entries (to cut/paste into sprint):
- RWI-4801: FE: compact route card — collapsed view + sparkline — 3pts (Tomas)
- RWI-4802: BE: /routes/:id/summary mock endpoint — 2pts (Samir)
- RWI-4803: QA: smoke tests for route card expand + trace links — 1pt (Jin)
- RWI-4804: PM: copy + screenshot for support article — 1pt (Maya)

If time permits: prototype small in-console keyboard navigator to quickly accept/reject intake queue items (would be an accessibility win).

Slack refs: #console-product, #infra-telemetry.

End of doc.
